title: Earl Fawcett's band at the Carmel Club and trumpeter Joe Betty
summary: He joined Earl Fawcett at the Carmel Club; he recalls the leader's wife bringing food and playing drums, and trumpeter Joe Betty's drug use.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Tony, yeah. And what was it? Then I went with Earl Fawcett.

I started with him at the Carmel Club on Blyer Street. His wife used to come in and bring red beans and rice at night. Feed the band? And she played a drum while you eat. Oh, really? Oh, she'd bring his dinner?
Yeah, you had to bring your dinner on them jobs.
You had to bring two shirts.
Bring two shirts? You sweat, yeah.
And then she, was she a good drummer? Yeah, she played nice drums.

She played really nice drums. Yeah. She played time. Well, during that time Joe Betty was playing trumpet then. Nice trumpet player. But Joe Betty was using dope and every time he'd go on a job he'd pull his arm for that dope. That's for running him crazy. I've never seen Joe with a woman in my life. Never. And Joe was a good leader.
Yeah. And when did he die?
He's still in it? He's still in it. What's he doing?
Oh, he's, he come out for the preservation hall sometimes.
Yeah, well he's selling wheat but I got a wheat from him this week. He was passing the handbook.
Oh, yeah, sure. He was working at first in Daniel for drinks. Well, he doesn't play music anymore, though. No, no, no.
I'm not sure I said there was a good choice.
